commit.subject: fix(codex): name image generation and scripted image views

entries.text:
Task: harden how toolreader displays Codex sessions, testing against the real Codex CLI sessions on this machine. Report back what you found and fixed.

Context: toolreader (this repo, read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly, including "The ways to hurt yourself") is a read-only viewer of what coding agents did. It already lists and renders Codex sessions that ran outside T3 through `codex app-server` (src/server/CodexSessions.ts, src/core/codex.ts, src/core/normalize.ts). There are ~2600 Codex rollout files under <path>

Branch: you are on `feat/production-plan`. Create `fix/codex-display` from it and commit there. Do not touch master or push anything.

What to do:
1. Pick ~15 diverse real Codex sessions (interactive CLI, `codex exec`, long ones, ones with apply_patch / file edits, MCP tool calls, web search, failed commands, subagents, images, very large outputs, old and new rollout formats). For each, compare what the viewer shows (API `/api/threads/<id>` and the UI) against the raw rollout JSONL. Look for: missing or duplicated actions, wrong kinds/colors, wrong status (failed shown as ok), broken diffs, wrong timestamps/order, unreadable titles, items that degrade to untyped rows, crashes, slow loads.
2. Fix what is wrong, at the root cause, each with a focused unit test using a trimmed, anonymized payload (no real secrets or private paths in fixtures).
3. Known bug to fix too: shell commands quoted like '"'…'"' are parsed wrongly in src/core/shell.ts.
4. Run the server on PORT=4779 (never 4777) against a snapshot of the T3 DB as AGENTS.md "Test data" describes. Use the T3 preview browser tools to check the UI for the sessions you fixed. Stop only the server PID you started.
5. Verify: `vp test run`, `vp check`, `vp run typecheck`, `vp run build`. Commit in small conventional commits (git -c user.email=<private> commit), each ending with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Report: a table of sessions checked (id prefix, kind, what was wrong), the commits you made, and anything you found but did not fix.

Checking the remaining items: large outputs seem fine since a 46MB session loads quickly, and now I want to verify how imageGeneration and subAgentActivity-only sessions are handled, plus confirm whether the 31 old-format files without a type field are properly listed.
Main fix committed. Now the remaining categories from the brief: image generation items, the 31 oldest-format rollouts, and the UI. Check the first two:

The 31 oldest rollouts from August 2025 predate `session_meta` and aren't returned by `codex app-server thread/list`, so I'll report this limitation rather than build a separate reader for them. Now checking image generation.

entries.text:
I notice imageGeneration items get an untyped title currently, so I need to add a branch that detects this type and builds a proper title like "generate image: ..." using a shortened version of the revised prompt, since the type mapping already routes it as an image view tool action.

I also want to catch the case where a script calls view_image directly without a nested ImageView item—using a regex to pull the path argument out so it can still be rendered as an imageView. It's a small addition but cheap to include, so I'll implement both fixes along with tests.
Image generation renders as an untyped `imageGeneration` row, and a script whose only job is `tools.view_image` shows as raw script. Tests first:

entries.text:
Since exec-2 has no recorded line in the v1 scan, it gets an effective sequence number that sorts before v1's entry, since exec-2's timestamp equals the creation time while v1's is later. That means exec-2 should come first, so I need to flip my expected ordering to put exec-2 before read.

Now I'll add a revisedPrompt optional field to CodexItem in payload.ts, branch the normalize logic for imageGeneration, and handle scriptImage extraction in the rollout code.
Now implement (expected order in the test: the thread/read item has no rollout line, so it sorts first; I'll fix that expectation):
